newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin - no justification for new auto incentives.
newsitem.headline: Jospin - no justification for new auto incentives.

text.p: Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said on Thursday he did not believe there was justification to revive car-buying incentives in France.

"It doesn't seem that what we're seeing in the French market justifies measures like the so-called Balladurettes or Juppettes," he said on France 2 television, referring to new-cars-for-old rebates put in place by previous governments.

"It seems because those measures artificially inflated the market while they were in effect that we're now seeing a brutal fall -- a drop of 30 percent in the French market ... Thankfully, it looks better on the export front," he said.
"So I don't believe in such measures," Jospin said, but added that the industry players should study the outlook.
The French carmakers' association CCFA said new car sales in France fell 30.7 percent in June from year-earlier levels when the rebates were in effect.
